text:
sasha: quick question — I'm wiring ExternalSecrets for the payments service and want to confirm the preferred Vault path format and rotation approach. I have some legacy code using `secret/data/services/payments` and a kube secret named `payments-api`.

miguel: for ExternalSecrets (external-secrets.io) we normally reference the KV v2 logical path without `/data` in the CRD. so use `secret/services/payments` as the `remoteRef.key` and set `property: api_key`. ExternalSecrets handles the API translation.

sasha: ah ok makes sense. can you show a tiny snippet of the CRD we want in the helm values?

miguel: sure — something like:
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: payments-credentials
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1m
  secretStoreRef:
    name: redwood-vault
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: payments-api
  data:
    - secretKey: API_KEY
      remoteRef:
        key: secret/services/payments
        property: api_key
```

sasha: thanks. what about TTL/rotation? the token in Vault is long-lived for infra right now. we want autosync so k8s secrets get rotated when Vault rotates.

emma: two cases:
1) static secrets in KV: Vault doesn't auto-rotate KV entries. set `refreshInterval` on ExternalSecret (we use 1m or 5m depending on traffic) and push rotations via CI / manual Vault ops.
2) dynamic secrets (DB/kv plugins): if you use Vault's database or dynamic secrets engine, Vault issues short-lived creds — ExternalSecrets will fetch them on refresh so k8s secret TTL is effectively the dynamic TTL. So if you need automatic rotation use dynamic engine.

sasha: good point. for payments we can move the api key rotation to a job that writes a new KV entry monthly. external-secrets will pick it up within `refreshInterval`. any gotchas with `refreshInterval` too low?

miguel: watch rate limits and Vault request surge. 1m is fine for low-cardinality secrets, but if you have many pods/secrets set a higher interval or use cache/sidecar. Also set `policy` on Vault role to limit read scope.

jin: also remember to use k8s auth for Vault access (serviceAccount + role binding). don't mount tokens. our ClusterSecretStore should point at the Vault auth path and kubernetes auth role. example values in cluster secret store:
```yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterSecretStore
spec:
  provider:
    vault:
      server: https://vault.internal.redwood
      path: kubernetes
      auth:
        kubernetes:
          role: external-secrets-role
```

emma: +1. and on the Vault side create a policy like `path "secret/data/services/payments" { capabilities = ["read"] }` and bind to the `external-secrets-role`. keep policies narrow.

sasha: ok. last bit — helm values change: do we add `refreshInterval` per-service or centralize?

miguel: we usually set a sane default in the chart (`1m` or `5m`) and allow override per ExternalSecret. put secrets with different rotation needs in their own ES CR.

sasha: great, I'll update the helm chart and open a PR. pinging @jin for a quick review on the ClusterSecretStore patch.

deploy-bot: staged deploy for `infra/helm` started (uuid: 9c3a).

jin: i'll take a look this afternoon, also check Vault policy in your PR notes. small nit — use `target.template.type: kubernetes.io/basic-auth` if you need username/password mapping.

sasha: perfect, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
